messages.content: Who are the famous dancers of the 19th Century?

function.name: get_museum_artists
function.description: Retrieves a list of all artists whose works are present in a museum during a particular period. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

period.description: The time period for which to retrieve the artists, e.g., 19th Century.

country.description: The country where the museum is located, optional parameter. Default: 'USA'

message.content:
Here are some of the most celebrated dancers who made their mark in the 19th century:

| Dancer | Nationality | Notable Contributions |
|--------|-------------|-----------------------|
| **Marie Taglioni** (1804–1884) | Swiss/Italian | Pioneered the “en pointe” technique; famed for her ethereal style in *La Sylphide* (1832). |
| **Fanny Elssler** (1810–1879) | Austrian | Known for her virtuoso footwork and dramatic expressiveness; popularized the Viennese waltz on stage. |
| **Marius Petipa** (1818–1910) | Russian | Though primarily a choreographer, he also danced; his work laid foundations for classical ballet repertoire. |
| **Carlo Blasis** (1825–1901) | Italian | A leading male dancer and teacher; helped spread the French school of ballet across Europe. |
| **Anna Pavlova** (1881–1931) | Russian | While she rose to fame slightly later, her early training began in the late 19th century; she would become one of the era’s most iconic ballerinas. |
| **Jean Coralli** (1797–1868) | French | Renowned for his choreography and as a principal dancer; collaborated with Jules Perrot on *Giselle*. |
| **Jules Perrot** (1793–1875) | French | Both choreographer and dancer; created many ballets that remain classics today. |
| **Eugène Scribe** (1793–1861) | French | Though more famous as a librettist, he worked closely with dancers in operas and ballets of the time. |

These performers were instrumental in shaping the evolution of ballet and dance during the 19th century, influencing both performance styles and the development of modern dance techniques.
